title: narcissus asturiensis subsp. villarvildensis
intro: Narcissus asturiensis subsp. villarvildensis, commonly known as the Spanish narcissus or wild daffodil, is a type of flowering plant belonging to the Amaryllidaceae family. This plant has been used for centuries in traditional medicine due to its numerous health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties, which can aid in wound healing and reduce pain. The therapeutic actions of Narcissus asturiensis subsp. villarvildensis include its ability to act as a natural analgesic, antispasmodic, and anti-inflammatory agent, making it useful for treating various conditions such as arthritis and respiratory issues. The bioactive constituents responsible for these effects include alkaloids, glycosides, and phenolic compounds, specifically galantamine, which has been shown to have neuroprotective properties and is used in the treatment of Alzheimer's disease.
